claim_quote.original: in allen europäischen Ländern fünf- bis fünfzehnmal mehr Todesfälle durch Kälte als durch Hitze
claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: in all European countries five to fifteen times more deaths from cold than from heat
claim_quote.underline: allen europäischen Ländern fünf- bis fünfzehnmal

counter_quote.original: Country-level annual excess number of deaths

locator.section: Corrected Table 2, Denmark, Finland, UK and Croatia rows

correction: Describe the corrected study’s estimates for adults aged 20 and older in 854 urban areas during 2000–2019. Its country-grouped point estimates imply cold/heat ratios of about 31.6 for Denmark (884/28), 32.3 for Finland (1452/45), 58.1 for the UK (28342/488), and 3.9 for Croatia (1142/293). They do not support an everywhere-five-to-fifteen description. The corrected German ratio 12108/2015 is about 6.0.
effect: Corrects the universal numerical range in a supporting health comparison. The deviations are mixed, the study still estimates a larger aggregate cold burden, and the approximate German six-to-one ratio is supported within its urban cohort. No uniform direction of policy advantage is established.
limits: This is a narrow overgeneralisation of cited evidence, not proof of a different whole-population ratio in every country. The estimates are modelled temperature-attributable mortality with uncertainty, not counts of direct hypothermia and heatstroke deaths. The study was corrected on 2 July 2024; corrected values are used. A historical cold/heat comparison does not by itself determine the effect of future warming, adaptation or emissions policy.
context_and_alternatives: Researcher A and both independent final reviewers B and C re-read all nine physical pages; root read the full text and visually inspected physical page 6.
The separate German approximately-six comparison is numerically consistent with corrected Table 2; its nationwide generalisation remains a separate unresolved ledger assessment.
The original article’s age 85+ code error changed impact levels. A 2 July 2024 correction notice and corrected article are archived; the superseded institutional copy is preserved as history.
The surrounding argument concerns whether warming reduces mortality and whether wind energy is more harmful. This correction does not establish either broader conclusion.

The corrected aggregate ratio is about 9.58 and lies inside five to fifteen. An approximate aggregate comparison is fair, but does not support the explicit every-country range. Point-estimate ratios are checked without inventing ratio confidence intervals from marginal bounds.
materiality_explanation: Minor: corrects a universal numerical range and the population scope of a supporting health comparison. It preserves the cited study’s larger aggregate cold burden and does not independently decide the policy request.
direction_explanation: Unknown: the universal range supports a health comparison used in the abolition argument, but the table’s deviations are mixed. The claim understates several northern cold/heat ratios and overstates Croatia’s ratio. Correcting the range does not uniformly weaken or strengthen the policy case.

confidence.text_source_mismatch: High for the corrected table and universal-range description; actual national population ratios are not established here.
